goal: Convert the latest research into a controlled next step for training a standalone Arabic retriever without blindly scaling the below-gate v62 recipe.

current_best_system_reference.experiment: v56 BGE-M3 hybrid r100 + BGE-reranker-v2-m3 min-max blend
current_best_system_reference.claim_boundary: retrieval-system result, not standalone embedding-model SOTA

current_best_standalone_student_diagnost.experiment: v62 official no-DDP BGE-M3 unified head-only student smoke
current_best_standalone_student_diagnost.diagnostic: fixed v52-v54 same-candidate MIRACL Arabic gate
current_best_standalone_student_diagnost.decision: below gate; do not scale or publish

fresh_sources_checked.implication: Standalone student should preserve dense, sparse, and multi-vector modes and use teacher-score distillation rather than dense-only training.
Official inference example fuses dense, sparse, and ColBERT scores with weights [0.4, 0.2, 0.4].
Official fine-tuning supports knowledge distillation from pos_scores and neg_scores, exposes score temperature, and supports m3_kd_loss.
Training-time M3 compute_score defaults to dense=1.0, sparse=0.3, ColBERT=1.0, which may not match the current evaluation fusion surface.
Qwen3 remains a mandatory instruction-aware high-end baseline and teacher/reranker reference, but not a replacement for a self-owned student checkpoint.
ArabicMTEB is the best Arabic-centric SOTA target, but reproducible artifacts still need verification before same-harness claims.

fresh_sources_checked.source: Swan and ArabicMTEB Hugging Face paper page
fresh_sources_checked.implication: Community comments indicate users still struggle to find the Swan model and ArabicMTEB benchmark artifacts, so current claims must stay conservative.
A public standalone-model claim should produce standard MTEB result files and model metadata; the current v56 stack should not be submitted as an embedding checkpoint.

research_findings: The strongest public Arabic-centric target is Swan/ArabicMTEB, but it is currently a paper-level reference rather than a clean reproducible baseline for this repo.
BGE-M3 remains the best practical student base because its paper and official model card align with the teacher system's dense+sparse+multi-vector structure.
The immediate technical uncertainty is not row count; it is whether v62 was trained and evaluated on mismatched score-weight and temperature surfaces.
A checkpoint improvement must be measured against the base model under the same candidate pool and same fusion weights; otherwise the result is only a scoring-system ablation.

next_controlled_diagnostic.name: v63 weight-and-temperature alignment diagnostic
stage_a_no_training: Re-evaluate base BGE-M3 and v62 head checkpoint on the fixed same-candidate MIRACL Arabic gate under identical fusion weights.
Include [0.4, 0.2, 0.4], normalized [1.0, 0.3, 1.0], sparse-heavy, dense-heavy, and ColBERT-heavy grids.
Require the student to beat the base under the same weights by at least +0.005 nDCG@10 before treating it as a model gain.
stage_b_training_only_if_stage_a_support: Run a small lower-learning-rate official no-DDP M3 smoke.
Align training score temperature with the best diagnostic surface.
Prefer staged sparse-then-ColBERT or base-anchored training over simply increasing row count.
stage_c_broader_validation: If the gate passes, evaluate on a held-out candidate-pool split before full MIRACL dev.
Then expand to MKQA/Mr.TyDi/Namaa/ArabicMTEB-reproducible tasks before any SOTA wording.

decision.next_action: Implement or run the v63 same-candidate fusion-weight diagnostic before any new training.
